did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the very beginning of the chapter, David describes God's knowledge as personal and intimate: God searches him and knows him.

Did you know? In verses 1–6, the psalm emphasizes that God knows a person's movements, thoughts, and even words that have not yet been spoken: “You know when I sit and when I rise” and “There is not a word on my tongue.”
Did you know? David asks whether it is possible to move away from God's Spirit or presence, and concludes that there is nowhere a person can flee from Him.

Did you know? The image “I rise on the wings of the dawn” describes an attempt to reach vast distances, even “the far side of the sea”; yet there too, according to the psalm, God's hand will guide and hold the person.
Did you know? In verses 11–12, darkness is not seen as something that can hide a person from God: “Even the darkness will not be dark to You,” and before God, the night shines like the day.
Did you know? David connects God's knowledge with his personal creation: God formed his inmost being and covered him while he was still in his mother's womb.
Did you know? The psalm describes God as seeing a person even in his unformed state, before his development is complete, and notes that all his days were written in God's book.
Did you know? God's thoughts are described as precious and extremely numerous, so many that David compares their number to the grains of sand; even when he awakens, he is still with God.

Did you know? The chapter ends with a request for self-examination: David asks God to search his heart, examine his thoughts, identify any harmful way within him, and guide him in the everlasting way.
